result.rule: When the description states that one participant communicates information to another participant and separately describes the recipient’s later reaction, arrival, or other action: Model the communication with a message flow from the sending participant’s communication element to an element that represents receipt of that communication; model the recipient’s later reaction or action separately in that participant’s process.

When the description states that one participant communicates with another participant or transfers an item to them: Model the message flow between elements that represent the described sender and receiver. Use a receiving event as an endpoint only when it represents receipt of that communication; do not substitute an unrelated activity or event for either endpoint.
When the description states that a participant performs a distinct activity after a condition is met: Model the activity as a BPMN task and connect it to the surrounding process flow.

When the description states that an artifact or information is sent from one participant to another and specifies a communication channel: Label the modeled sending activity from the responsible sender’s perspective and include the specified channel in its label.

args.text: When the description explicitly presents mutually exclusive outcomes as alternatives, model the decision with an exclusive gateway and connect each alternative to its corresponding path.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers modeling explicit alternative outcomes with an exclusive gateway.

result.rule: When the description states that a process can end with one of several mutually exclusive outcomes: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway and connect each outgoing branch to the activity or end event corresponding to that outcome.

When the description gives alternative outcomes for handling an individual item, followed by a check of the larger set and a decision about whether to continue processing items: Connect each alternative outcome path to the shared check. Model an explicitly described check as an activity before a condition-based gateway, and route the gateway’s outcomes to the described continuation or completion paths.

When the description states that the outcome of an evaluation determines whether further activities are required: Model an exclusive gateway after the activity that evaluates the outcome, with branches for whether the further activities are required.

When the description says that a person selects an option and that subsequent actions depend on which option was selected: Model the selection as an activity, then use a gateway to route the resulting alternatives.

args.text: When the description says one participant sends a message or item to another participant, model the sending activity using an appropriate BPMN communication element rather than treating it as an absent activity.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already covers modeling a described sending activity and the choice of BPMN element.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
